records.public_safe_text: this is traffic fatality #67 for the city of dallas in 2025. unit 1 was [roadway]. unit 2(a pedestrian) was [roadway] in the north cross walk. unit 1 collided with unit 2. unit 2 went airborne and came to rest on [roadway] [roadway]. unit 1 fled the location without providing the required information. investigating officer observed video of unit 1 prior to the collision. however, at the time this report was entered, no calculations had been done. at this time, investigating officer was unable to determine which unit had right of way[medical facility] by dfr rescue #11. unit 2 was pronounced deceased at 3:02 am by the attending physician. the medical examiner's office was contacted on me# 25-11813. all body worn camera and photos were uploaded and saved to evidence. com on incident #25-1326300. this investigation is incomplete pending the identification of unit 1 and unit 1 driver as well as unit 2's blood toxicology results. see related report [phone] ********** this report was supplemented by the vehicle crimes unit detective (i/o) assigned to investigate this crash/offense. i/o added the information for unit 1, unit 1 driver and unit 1 front right passenger. the investigation showed that unit 1 was traveling at speed much higher than the posted speed limit of 35mph, when he struck unit 2 pedestrian, therefore i/o added the contributing factor of 61 - speeding over the limit to unit 1. unit 2 pedestrian had a contributing factor of 98 on the original report, but due to unit 1's speed, the contributing factor of 98 was removed from unit 2 pedestrian. the texas department of transportation (txdot) added the alcohol results in unit 2 pedestrian, prior to this supplement. i/o has not been able to physically obtain unit 1 and inspect the damages, so this report will remain incomplete. **********

records.deidentified_narrative: unit #1 and its towed #2 were traveling eastbound on ih 30 [roadway] [roadway] as they approached the construction work zone. unit #3, an orange and black 2024 kubota svl-97-2 skid steer forklift (pin kbcz064chr1d84937), was traveling southbound in the grassy median toward the eastbound lanes of ih 30. unit #3 was part of a construction crew repairing the metal guardrail to the north of the roadway. a construction pickup towing a trailer outfitted with a crash attenuator and directional board with the four corner lights activated was stationary just to the north of the eastbound lanes and to the west of the guardrail facing east and partially obstructing unit #3's view. unit #4 was traveling eastbound on ih 30 [roadway] behind units #1 and #2. unit #5, a construction worker, was on the roadway side of the guardrail attempting to pick up traffic cones. unit #3 turned when unsafe and attempted to cross both eastbound lanes between the pickup and guardrail. unit #1 swerved to the right but struck unit #3's right side with unit #1's front left. unit #3 began to spin counterclockwise ejecting the [roadway]. unit #3 then struck unit #2's left front quarter with unit #3's right back quarter. unit #3 came to [roadway] [roadway] facing east. unit #1 then struck the metal guardrail to the south of the roadway with unit #1's front right. units #1 and #2 came to rest [roadway] and the eastbound shoulder. unit #4 then struck the driver of unit #3 dragging him before coming to a [roadway] facing east with the driver of unit #3 underneath. unit #5 was struck by debris from the crash causing injury. the driver of unit #[medical facility] in mount pleasant where he was later pronounced deceased. autopsy toxicology results were negative. photographs were taken. the insurance information for unit #3 is ohio indemnity ([phone]), policy number 0001192944619pdp11.

records.deidentified_narrative: on the listed date and time, i was in full uniform on marked patrol with lightbar affixed to the rooftop, when police responded to the listed business location for an accident major - pedestrian involved. upon arrival, i made contact with u3 and u4 (juvenile pedestrians and brothers) as well as u3 and u4's parents. u3 and u4 were being treated by safd (ems) on scene. i made contact with u3 and u4's parents and spoke through a spanish speaking officer (i am not a spanish speaker). u3 and u4's parents stated that u1 crashed into u2 (parked) and pushed u2 into u3 and u4, running over both of the pedestrians. u4's mother was holding him, while u3 was being placed in the back of an ambulance for transport. i made contact with u1 driver who was emotionally disturbed and had multiple persons angry with her. for her safety and for a cooling off period for herself, i placed her in the back of a patrol vehicle without handcuffs and advised her that she was not under arrest. u1 stated she dropped off her father at the store front, then circled the lot until she observed an open parking space which butted up against the parking space where u2 was parked. u1 driver stated her father had been driving u1 and is much taller than her, so the driver seat was placed further back than where she would have it. u1 driver stated that she did not adjust the seat before driving through the parking lot, then when she was pulling into the parking space, she pressed down for the brake pedal, but because of the seat being too far away, was unable to depress it far enough to stop the vehicle. u1 driver stated u1's front bumper then crashed into u2's front bumper resulting in the listed damage and resulting in u2 being pushed out of it's parking space. i did not observe any signs of impairment or intoxication from u1 driver at this time. i then made contact with heb employees who stated they have video of the incident. in the surveillance video, i observed u3 and u4 walking soutbound through the parking lot away from the building. i observed u2 parked facing southwest bound in a parking [roadway] northbound through the parking lot, then pull into a parking space facing u2, but then fail to slow down or come to a stop. i observed u1 crash into u2, pushing both u1 and u2 [roadway]. i observed u2 crash into and run over u3 but only crash into u4. i then advised ems of the details of the video, so they could more accurately address and treat all medical related issues of the pedestrians. shortly after, safd [medical facility] for treatment but stated the on-scene prognosis was non-life threatening. u2 owner had arrived on scene and observed the damage to her vehicle. all parties were issued sapd [case id] with contact information for insurance purposes. dmea

(involved)offense(s): leaving scene of accidentmedia/document(s): bwc uploaded into evidence. com, cris crash report completed. narrative: on 18august 2025, i was assigned to the hays county sheriffs office, uniformed patrol division, shift iv supervisor (east). on this date, at approximately 1855 hours, hays county law enforcement was dispatched [roadway] & [roadway], buda, hays county, texas. deputies were dispatched to this location regarding a 10-minute delayed vehicle versus pedestrian collision. deputies yrazouqui and deleon arrived on scene and established contact with jeremi mason (w/m dob: [date]). jeremi informed law enforcement and 911 call taker that an older model white dodge pickup truck struck him, while he [roadway]. i was contacted via phone call by deputy deleon whilst i traveled to the scene. i was informed that jeremi alleged to have been struck by a dodge ram pickup (older model) that was white [roadway] he [roadway] which made law enforcement believe he was walking on the ih 35 [roadway], speed limits are approximately 50 miles per hour. jeremi claimed his already broken arm was struck via a vehicle, as he walked along side of the roadway. i was further advised that there were no signs of obvious injury or trauma, aside from a cast on his right arm, that appeared to have been placed by medical personnel other than ems. i was advised that ems did not see any signs of trauma other than this cast, nor were there any signs that jeremi had struck the ground (road rash, grass clippings, or other vegetation). i arrived on scene and spoke with jeremi. this was done due to the reported call being a hit and run accident against a pedestrian. in normal cases, a department of public safety trooper would be summoned to the scene. due to possible credibility issues with statement, i believed that further interview & analysis would be needed prior to utilizing state law enforcement for this investigation. it should be noted that for the past few months, hays county texas area has had limited state trooper presence and a majority of them are on call status. while speaking with jeremi, i was informed that he had previously been struck via a vehicle while [roadway], between manchaca & buda texas. on todays date, he was walking on the roadway, within the path of travel of vehicles, and towards on coming traffic. utilizing google maps, we identified the accident location as being the 690 block of hillside terrace. while walking west bound on hillside terrace (south side of roadway), in between white lines, jeremi indicated that he was waving his arms notifying on coming vehicles he was in the roadway. most vehicles yielded to him however the older white dodge described by him struck him with its passenger side. jeremi was heard indicating that the impact caused him to fall to the ground. i was informed that based on his knowledge of texas transportation code, and state law, if there was no side walk present, he should walk against the flow of traffic, to the left side of the roadway. it should be noted that this area of hillside terrace does not have side walks. the south side of hillside terrace is immediately apparent as not being safe. on the north side of the roadway, there is an approximate 20-30 feet worth of grassy area, that would serve as a safe area to commute on. this area is between a fence line and the roadway and does not bear any no trespass notices and is immediately apparent as public easement. i explained to jeremi what my experience and knowledge of the statute regarding pedestrians walking on roadways, and how that grassy area to the north side would be much more in line with the spirit of the law. the south side of the roadway had no shoulder, approximately 1-3 feet worth of shoulder. this roadway is approximately 40 mile per hour speed limit zone. these factors make walking along the south side of hillside terrace objectively unsafe, when compared to the north side. as i continued to speak with jeremi, i learned that he recently became homeless and was a recovering methamphetamine addict. i was advised that he used to use methamphetamine daily prior to starting his sobriety. jeremi further advised that he was already working on receiving victims compensation for the prior reported hit and run accident which allegedly led to his broken arm. jeremi advised that this prior accident and now this current situation has kept and will keep him from gainful employment. jeremi appeared to be in a disheveled state with clothes appearing dirty and soiled. he was observed carrying a large gym bag, and his appearance was that of a transient. i instructed deputy yrazouqui to travel to the area of 690 hillside terrace, and search for video surveillance systems. on camera was located, however it was directed onto private property, and the angle would [roadway] side events. jeremi also advised multiple people to stop by to see to his needs after the accident, however no additional calls were received regarding this accident. based on the totality of the circumstances, i observed no articulable evidence to indicate that this event did or did not in fact happen. only jeremis statements support the occurrence of this event. i observed a potential and reasonable belief that this report may be filled by jeremi with intent to obtain financial benefit, however this belief is only based on lack of evidence. based on the totality of the, and lack of additional workable leads or clues, this case will be inactivated. end of report (inactive)

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] at approximately 1411 hours, while on patrol at san antonio college (sac) [roadway], san antonio, tx 78212, police responded to [roadway] [roadway] for a report of a pedestrian (unit 1), that was hit by a vehicle (unit 2). we made location at 1320 hours, and san antonio fire department (safd) medic # 4 case was on scene. safd was ensuring unit 1 had no major injuries. san antonio police department (sapd) was also on scene. i immediately requested dispatch to check the license plate unit 2 through ncic/tcic. dispatch confirmed unit 2 had active insurance. i asked the dispatcher to check the driver of unit 2 through ncic/tcic because the driver only presented a texas identification card. dispatch informed me unit 2 driver did not have any wants or warrants but he did not have a driver license. i reported this information to responding officer. i told unit 2 that i would be issuing him a san antonio traffic violation citation for transportation code 521. 02 - license [roadway] date would be on october 6, 2025. unit 2 signed the citation [roadway]. i returned his texas identification card and vehicle insurance. unit 1 refused medical [medical facility]. responding officer requested dispatch to check unit 1 through ncic/tcic with the information unit 1 provided; dispatch could not confirm. responding officer then detained unit 1 for failure to identify. unit 1 then advised us unit 1 was from out of state. i asked the dispatcher to recheck unit 1s information, and they advised unit 1 had no wants or warrants. responding officer then detained unit 1 for an emergency detention. unit 1 appeared to not be in a right state of mind because unit 1 had clear injuries to her head, unit 1 was stating unit 1 was a police officer, but unit 1 was not, and because unit 1 walked into busy traffic causing an accident and injuries. if unit 1 was left alone, there would be reason to believe unit 1 would hurt herself or others. assisting officer arrived on scene and assisted by taking custody of unit 1. assisting office [medical facility], later, i contacted witnesses 1 and witness 2 for more of their information since they saw unit 1 walk into traffic and cause an accident with unit 2. my body camera was activated.

records.deidentified_narrative: on wednesday, [date], at approximately 1510 hours, i officer r. govea #1907 with the wallis pd was dispatched to a crash in the 6607 block commerce, wallis, texas. once on location, i spoke with the victim that was hit of unit #2 inside of the business of [roadway] wallis, texas 77485 identified as jantzen, kaylyn elizabeth, w/f, dob [date], txdl 45508157, [roadway], wallis, tx 77485 who advised she was driving her electric scooter described as a black askgo riding king which had no damage after the accident was [roadway] on the shoulder. when [roadway] 60 [roadway], she observed a white in color ram pickup bearing txlp [identifier] to be stopped at the yield sign so she continued. while continuing she was then struck by the white ram that was [roadway] 60 and commerce facing east turning right to head south on commerce. prior to my arrival med 4 was enroute and jantzen wanted to be checked by them due to her having a bump on her head and falling. i then went to speak with the driver of the white ram who was identified as alviar, isaac h/m dob [date], txdl 47370276, [roadway] bay city, texas 77414. when i asked alviar what happened he stated he was at the yield sign [roadway] 60 onto commerce to head south but when he began to move forward, he struck jantzen which caused her to fall from [roadway] and hit her head. i asked did he not see her or what was the cause of it. alviar then stated he did not see her and she came out of nowhere, i asked about how fast was he going in which he stated no more than 5 mph due to him just releasing the brake and proceeding to turn onto commerce. i then took photos of the vehicle bearing txlp [identifier] and when observing for any damage no damage was done, a picture of the insurance was also taken and placed in this case file, after gathering all information needed, i had alviar fill out a voluntary statement form as well as for jantzen and placed it in this case file along with a total of 16 photos of the vehicles and photos of jantzen's injuries. after gathering all information needed, i advised alviar he would be receiving a citation for fail to yield right of way (intersection), alviar was given citation #73859 and jantzen was transported to [medical facility] katy, i officer r. govea #1907 checked back in service with this crash report.

records.deidentified_narrative: on 21 aug 2025 approx 2:35p, unit 1 was [roadway] [roadway] [roadway]. unit 2 was being chased on foot by unit 3, a garland police officer in full uniform. units 2 and 3 were traveling east across both south and north bound lanes of the [roadway]. as unit 1 neared units 2 and 3, unit 2 failed to yield the right of way to unit 1 [roadway] of travel. unit 2 was struck on his right leg by unit 1's front right bumper. unit 2 continued to travel across the north bound lanes and into a creekbed located on the east side of the roadway. unit 3, who was on foot and in pursuit of unit 2 also entered into the path of unit 1. unit 3 was able to avoid the front left and left distributed of unit 1, but struck the left back quarter. after striking unit 1, unit 3 continued the pursuit of unit 2. the driver of unit 1 left the crash site after both unit 2 and 3 disappeared from the crash site and into the creek bed. ofc crockett was notified of crash via patrol supervisor.
